case_name: Somesh Tiwari v Union Of India And Others
facts: The basic fact of the matter is not in dispute. Appellant is an officer of Indian Revenue Service. He was posted as a Deputy Commissioner of Central Excise at Bhopal.
An anonymous complaint was made alleging caste-bias on his part, pursuant whereto an order of transfer was passed against him on or about 22nd August, 2005.
He indisputably made a representation praying that on compassionate and humanitarian grounds, he may be retained at Bhopal for at least one year.
By an order dated 27th September, 2005, having regard to the fact that the representation filed by the appellant had not been disposed of by the authorities of the respondents, it was directed :-
The said representation was rejected by an order dated 19th October, 2005, and another representation was filed by the appellant on or about 25th October, 2005.

During the pendency of the said O.A., respondents while considering the matter of promotion, posting and transfer in the grade of the Assistant Commissioner of Customs and Central Excise, passed order dated 28th December, 2005 inter alia transferring/posting on administrative consideration, transferred the appellant from Shillong to Ahmedabad.
The orders under challenge before the Tribunal were, thus, the orders dated 22nd August, 2005 ; 19th October, 2005 and 28th December, 2005.
issues: Whether the High Court while quashing an order of transfer passed against the appellant was correct in directing that he would not be entitled to salary for the period commencing 15 days after the modified order of transfer to Ahmedabad was passed till the date he again joined his duties at the original place.
Whether the order of transfer could be passed on the basis of an anonymous complaint, which on enquiry having been found to be incorrect.
Whether the transfer of the petitioner on the ground that he apparently gave an impression that he worked on caste-biased ideology was unjustified.
petitioner_arguments: He should be retained at Bhopal for at least one year due to compassionate and humanitarian grounds.
The anonymous complaint against him was not found to be true during the enquiry.
The order of transfer was passed as a punishment, which is unjustified.
The petitioner has fundamental rights under Article 14, 15(1) and 16(2) of the Constitution of India.
respondent_arguments: The order of transfer was passed on administrative exigencies.
The applicant has All India transfer liability.
The authorities can extract service of the applicant wherever they want.
The impugned orders were within the purview of the respondents' powers.
court_reasoning: The Tribunal need not interfere with the impugned orders.
There is no illegality or irregularity committed by the Respondents while passing the impugned orders.
The order of transfer could not be passed on the basis of an anonymous complaint, which on enquiry having been found to be incorrect.
The transfer of the petitioner on the ground that he apparently gave an impression that he worked on caste-biased ideology was unjustified.
